rows.comment: Carlsson didn't participate in Sunday's practice after getting injured in Saturday's 3-2 loss to Utah. He might not be available for Monday's matchup against Seattle. Carlsson has registered seven goals, 29 points and 41 shots on net in 24 outings this season.

Anaheim recalled Nico Myatovic from AHL San Diego in a corresponding move. Sennecke will miss at least the next three games, starting with Saturday's matchup against Utah, but it's unclear when he will be available to return. He has registered 12 goals, 26 points, 53 shots on net and 19 hits in 22 appearances this season.

Poehling is on long-term injured reserve, but he is eligible to be activated at any time. He's still expected to be out until early December, though he may beat that timeline by a small margin if his recovery continues to go well.

Greer suffered an upper-body injury in Sunday's 6-3 win over Ottawa. He will miss at least the next four games, starting with Tuesday's matchup against Vancouver, but it's unclear when he will be ready to return. Greer has four goals, six points, 23 shots on net and 36 hits in 13 appearances this season.

After being placed on injured reserve early Saturday morning, Hagens' timeline for recovery has been revealed to keep him sidelined for at least the next five or six games. It's an unfortunate break for the Bruins and the 20-year-old winger, as he had posted six goals, 12 points, 34 shots on net and 19 blocked shots over 17 games prior to going down. His absence might hurt his rookie of the year case in the long run, but once he's able to return, he'll give the Bruins' third line a major boost. In his absence, expect the newly recalled Michael Eyssimont, who was named the AHL's player of the month for October, to take his place.

Danforth's move to IR allowed the Sabres to activate Sam Carrick (middle body) ahead of Thursday's game versus the Ducks. Danforth remains without a clear timeline to return to action. He will miss his fourth straight game Thursday and will be eligible to return whenever ready, as long as he doesn't later end up on long-term injured reserve.

Buffalo placed Grzelcyk on injured reserve Tuesday. He hasn't played since Opening Night against Columbus on Oct. 1. With Rasmus Dahlin (upper body) and Grzelcyk unavailable, the Sabres recalled Dennis Gilbert from AHL Rochester to play against Montreal on Tuesday.

Pospisil suffered the injury on a high hit from Chicago's  Wyatt Kaiser late in the second period. The 27-year-old Pospisil has a history of concussions, and he could miss some time. He had four hits and one shot on net over 7:57 of ice time in Saturday's contest before leaving.

Huberdeau played well in his first career AHL game. The 33-year-old is wrapping up the rehab process for his hip surgery. He can spend up to two weeks with the Wranglers on this conditioning loan, but if he continues to play well, he may not need the full amount of time before he's ready for his NHL season debut.

Bahl suffered the injury in pregame warmups before Friday's 5-3 loss to Anaheim. He will finish the 2026-27 campaign with one goal, one assist, 12 shots on net, 16 blocked shots and 22 hits in 16 appearances. The Flames placed Bahl on injured reserve before Sunday's matchup against Philadelphia and recalled Brayden Pachal from AHL Calgary.

Ehlers registered an assist, but he was also limited to 11:22 of ice time in Carolina's 7-4 win over Edmonton on Saturday. He has six goals and 22 points in 23 outings with the Hurricanes in 2026-27. Nicolas Deslauriers might draw into the lineup Sunday as a result of Ehlers' injury.

Kaiser won't be eligible to return until Chicago hosts Minnesota on Nov. 29. He has contributed two goals, five assists, 19 shots on net, 30 blocked shots and 20 hits in 23 appearances this season. With Kaiser unavailable, Kevin Korchinski will likely play against Vancouver on Sunday.

Chicago recalled Dominic Toninato from AHL Rockford in a corresponding move. Bedard is poised to undergo shoulder surgery, and a timeline for his return will be revealed after the procedure. In 15 appearances this season, he has registered seven goals, 18 points, 44 shots on net, 12 hits and seven blocked shots.

Byram was previously ruled out for Saturday's matchup against Calgary, and he won't be available for Sunday's matchup against Vancouver. It's also doubtful that he will join the team for Wednesday's contest against Seattle. It remains unclear when he will be ready to return.

MacKinnon wouldn't be ready until mid-February if that timetable proves to be accurate. It can't be overstated how important MacKinnon is to the Avalanche. He finished each of the previous four regular seasons with over 110 points, and he was well on his way towards another elite campaign after scoring 10 goals and 30 points through 20 appearances. Brock Nelson and Nazem Kadri are serving as the Avalanche's top two centers while MacKinnon is unavailable.

Myers is slated to miss his third consecutive game while recovering from an upper-body injury. When healthy, the 36-year-old blueliner has recorded two assists, 13 shots on net, 17 hits and 36 blocked shots over 20 appearances this season. In his absence, Kyle Burroughs will likely remain in the lineup on the Stars' third pairing.

Back has an assist, five hits and nine blocks in seven appearances this season. While he's not expected to play Thursday in Vegas, perhaps he'll be an option Sunday versus Pittsburgh or Wednesday against Nashville.

Dallas also recalled Kyle Burroughs from AHL Texas on Saturday and placed Lian Bichsel (lower body) on injured reserve. Capobianco hasn't played since Oct. 27 against New Jersey. He hasn't earned a point in five appearances this season, but he has registered three shots on net, three blocked shots and two hits.

Dallas also recalled Kyle Burroughs from AHL Texas on Saturday and moved Kyle Capobianco (leg) to long-term injured reserve. Bichsel is week-to-week after being injured in Thursday's 8-3 loss to Winnipeg. He has one assist, 10 shots on net, 24 blocked shots and 39 hits in 18 appearances this season.

The Stars placed Duchene on long-term injured reserve just before the start of the 2026-27 campaign. It remains unclear when he will return, but his new timeline could keep him out until at least mid-January. Duchene posted 16 goals, 45 points and 89 shots on net in 57 regular-season appearances for Dallas in 2025-26.

Montembeault hasn't yet appeared in a regular-season game during the 2026-27 campaign, as he sustained a lower-body injury during practice in early October and has been on injured reserve since then. The Canadiens indicated in late October that the netminder had been upgraded to day-to-day, but it's not yet clear when he'll be able to make his season debut. After making a career-high 62 regular-season appearances for Montreal during the 2024-25 campaign, the 30-year-old went 10-8-4 with a 3.43 GAA and .872 save percentage across 25 regular-season outings with the Canadiens last year. The Red Wings already have John Gibson and Daniil Tarasov in the crease, but Gibson hasn't been particularly sharp early in the year, so Montembeault will likely have an opportunity to compete for playing time once he's healthy.
day-to-day

Edvinsson is continuing to hold out for a new contract as a restricted free agent, with no clear end in sight. It's possible a trade materializes at some point, though he would still need to agree to terms on a new contract with a different NHL club. Last season, Edvinsson recorded nine goals and 16 assists in 72 regular-season contests.

Even though he has received clearance to play, he isn't expected to suit up for Sunday's matchup against St. Louis. He has already missed the last four games, including Saturday's 7-4 loss to Carolina.

Regula continues to work his way back from offseason surgery that caused him to miss the entire preseason. With the shift to LTIR, the 26-year-old defenseman can be expected to miss at least the next nine games, having already been out of action for one, though it could be longer, considering the team hasn't provided a specific update.

By moving Savoie to LTIR, the Oilers will get some cap relief while he is sidelined, as their injuries have started to pile up. The 22-year-old forward logged all 82 regular-season games in his rookie campaign, generating 18 goals and 19 assists, including seven power-play points. Considering Savoie is expected to miss at least the first two weeks of the season, fantasy managers probably shouldn't be expecting him to significantly outperform those numbers in 2026-27.

Andersen, who signed a one-year, $1 million contract with Edmonton in July, is still rehabbing from a knee injury. He posted a 16-14-5 record with a 3.05 GAA and an .874 save percentage in 35 appearances for Carolina during the 2025-26 regular season. Once he's ready to play in the 2026-27 campaign with the Oilers, Andersen could compete for starts with Tristan Jarry and Devon Levi.

Janmark underwent an undisclosed procedure earlier in the year, but he's currently shelved until further notice. The 33-year-old winger was limited in 2025-26, where he compiled a goal and eight points across 43 regular-season outings. In his absence, Mathieu Joseph and Max Jones are expected to serve as the team's left wingers in the bottom six to open the 2026-27 campaign.

Marchand is slightly behind Aleksander Barkov (knee) in terms of his potential return date. Barkov should be back in the fold within the next three games, per head coach Paul Maurice on Saturday. The 38-year-old Marchand has appeared in only two games this season and hasn't been in the lineup since Oct. 6 against the Kings.

Barkov has appeared in only two games this season and hasn't played since Oct. 1. However, he is close to returning to the lineup. Once activated by the Panthers from long-term injured reserve, Barkov should occupy a top-six role while seeing time on the power play and penalty kill.

It's a step in the right direction for Gadjovich, who hasn't played since Oct. 25, 2025, against the Golden Knights, missing over a year of action. Given his extended layoff, the winger's return to practice doesn't mean he will be returning soon. Still, Gadjovich should slot into a bottom-six role for the club once given the all-clear.
day-to-day
day-to-day
day-to-day

A timeline for Hughes' return remains unclear, but he won't play against Vancouver on Saturday and will miss Monday's matchup against San Jose. He has posted eight goals, 34 points, 63 shots on net and 19 blocked shots in 24 appearances this season.

Gustavsson will see his first action since May 5 against the Avalanche in the playoffs last year. Look for the netminder to start at least one of two games against AHL San Diego on Friday and Saturday, if not both contests. Once given the all-clear, Gustavsson will likely slot into the No. 2 role behind Jesper Wallstedt, which could see Calvin Pickard shifted to the minors.

Matheson missed six straight games before returning to the lineup against Boston on Thursday. However, he was back on the shelf for Saturday's 4-1 loss to Colorado and will need more time to recover from his lingering injury. The 32-year-old defenseman has one goal, four assists, 16 shots on net, 16 blocked shots and five hits in nine appearances this season. With Matheson out, Adam Engstrom and David Reinbacher could compete for playing time.

The Canadiens moved Anderson to the injured reserve list Sunday after he logged a season-low 10:46 of ice time in Saturday's 4-1 loss to Colorado. He has contributed eight goals, 12 points, 35 shots on net and 42 hits in 19 appearances this season. With Anderson and Chris Kreider (lower body) dealing with long-term injuries, Florian Xhekaj and Owen Beck could see regular minutes in Montreal's bottom-six forward group.

Demidov has been on injured reserve since Oct. 6, and he initially received a return timetable of 2-4 weeks. He's now at the end of that estimate, and while it's encouraging to see him skating on his own, he's still in a walking boot, per Eric Engels of Sportsnet. Demidov appears likely to miss at least a few more games, but another step in his recovery will occur once he's officially cleared to practice with his teammates.

After being placed on long-term injured reserve on Wednesday, Mantha underwent surgery Monday to repair a throat fracture. Prior to sustaining the injury, the 32-year-old winger posted five goals, 10 points, 21 shots on net and 11 hits over 17 appearances this season. In his absence, Amadeus Lombardi and Lenni Hameenaho will likely continue to serve as depth options in New Jersey's forward room.

Kovacevic's ankle issue has been revealed to be a high-ankle sprain, which commonly requires four weeks or more to come back from. Prior to sustaining the injury on Nov. 10 against the Jets, the 29-year-old blueliner posted two points, a plus-2 rating, 10 shots on net, 13 hits and eight blocked shots over 13 appearances. In his absence, Vladislav Kolyachonok, Declan Chisholm and Anton Silaev will be the depth options to fill Kovacevic's role in the lineup.

Casey began the season on non-roster injured reserve due to knee surgery. This move to LTIR doesn't change his timeline -- he's already missed enough time to be eligible to return. He was slated to miss 6-8 weeks, so don't expect him to be ready until late November at the earliest.
day-to-day

Bjorkstrand landed on injured reserve Friday due to his upper-body injury, which has been revealed to keep him sidelined for the foreseeable future. Prior to going down, the 31-year-old winger compiled seven goals, 11 points, a plus-2 rating, 30 shots on net and 14 hits over 22 appearances. His current timetable for return should get him back in the mix around late January or early February. In the meantime, Matt Rempe will likely see more consistent playing time moving forward.

Smits landed on injured reserve in early November, which has caused him to miss the Rangers' last five games. The 18-year-old blueliner appeared in 17 contests prior to going down, where posted a minus-2 rating, eight shots on net, 16 hits and 10 blocked shots while averaging 14:29 of ice time. Given his current time line, he's expected to return sometime between late January and March. In his absence, Matthew Robertson and Scott Morrow should continue to see depth roles on the blue line.

Although Veleno didn't participate in practice Friday, it was encouraging to see him on the ice ahead of the session. The 26-year-old has been on long-term injured reserve since early October, and he was initially expected to miss approximately three months, so it wouldn't be surprising to see the Rangers bring him along slowly as he continues his recovery process.

Shesterkin was hurt during Friday's game against the Capitals when his right leg got jammed into the post while returning to the crease on a scrambled play, and the Rangers ruled him out for the season a day later. He was placed on injured reserve Sunday, and the team has now provided some clarification on the exact nature of his injury. Dylan Garand is slated to serve as the Rangers' No. 1 option in the crease until Joonas Korpisalo (lower body) is back in action.
day-to-day

Burakovsky has yet to join his teammates on the ice since getting hurt in late October, but this is a positive step in the right direction for the 31-year-old winger. In his eight appearances this year, Burakovsky has yet to register a point, recording four blocks, three hits and three shots while averaging just 11:00 of ice time, a career-low mark.

Foegele has been sidelined since late October, and he initially carried a return timetable of 3-4 weeks. While he hasn't yet entered that window, the fact that he hasn't yet resumed skating suggests that he isn't particularly close to returning to game action. A better idea of the 30-year-old's timetable to return will likely come into focus once he's cleared to return to the ice.

Eklund's timeline would seem to indicate that he will be out of action until the calendar flips to 2027, though it's possible he makes a late-December return if on the early side of his timeline. While the 24-year-old winger is already on injured reserve, he could be a candidate for long-term injured reserve if the Senators need the cap space to make a move.

Grebenkin's upper-body injury has been revealed to be an issue with his back, which he has successfully had repaired. The 23-year-old winger is expected to miss the majority of the 2026-27 campaign, but his current timeline for return, barring any setbacks, projects him back sometime after the All-Star break in mid-February. When he does return, Grebenkin will look to build off a positive rookie campaign, where he compiled four goals, 14 points, 32 shots on net, 86 hits and 17 blocked shots across 55 regular-season outings in 2025-26.

Carlile is day-to-day and will miss at least one game. He has contributed three goals, six points, 28 shots on net, 33 blocked shots and 18 hits in 21 appearances this season. Spencer Stastney will replace Carlile in Sunday's lineup against the Stars.

Rust has been out of action for the Penguins' last 11 contests due to his lower-body injury. When healthy, the 34-year-old winger has played in seven contests in which he has notched three goals and two assists, including a pair of power-play points.

Pittsburgh moved Soderblom to injured reserve Wednesday, and he has already missed the last two games. It's unclear when he will be ready to return to the lineup. Soderblom has contributed one assist, five shots on net, four blocked shots and 15 hits in six appearances this season.

Graves will miss the beginning of the 2026-27 campaign, and it's unclear when he will be ready to return. He contributed one goal, 21 shots on net, 38 blocked shots and 23 hits in 22 regular-season appearances for Pittsburgh in 2025-26.

Chernyshov remains on injured reserve and has missed the last 11 games after blocking a shot in Ottawa on Oct. 22. While an exact timeline for Chernyshov's return to the lineup hasn't been established, it's probably reasonable to assume that he will be out until sometime in December.

Musty suffered an upper-body injury ahead of training camp and was expected to have a long-term absence. He's been on non-roster injured reserve to begin the regular season, and it's not yet clear when he'll be deemed healthy. Once the 21-year-old is cleared to return to game action, he'll presumably be sent to AHL San Jose.

The Sharks announced in mid-September that Keyser was facing a long-term absence due to an upper-body injury, so his placement on non-roster injured reserve isn't particularly surprising. Once he's cleared to return, the 27-year-old will likely report to AHL San Jose.

O'Brien has been on non-roster injured reserve since the start of the regular season, but he's been with the team in Seattle and has been skating off to the side recently. Despite the 19-year-old's recent on-ice activity, it doesn't appear as though he's particularly close to being cleared for game action.

McCann had one goal in five games before sitting out Saturday's 5-1 loss to Minnesota. He has earned five assists, eight points, 28 shots on net, three blocked shots and six hits in 11 appearances this season. With McCann unavailable, Kaapo Kakko moved up to the top line in Saturday's game.

Krug's move to long-term injured reserve was partially a financial decision, as it allows the Blues to exceed the salary cap by $4 million. The 35-year-old blueliner hasn't played since the 2023-24 campaign, but he hasn't officially ruled out a return. Regardless of when he decides to hang up his skates, the 13-year NHL veteran will be remembered as an excellent two-way player, as he currently sits at 483 points, 621 hits and 832 blocked shots across 778 regular-season outings.

Based on Tucker's timeline, he shouldn't be expected back until mid-November, though it could certainly be longer. With Logan Mailloux (hand) also sidelined long-term, Adam Jiricek could see an extended run on the blue line. For his part, even once cleared to play, Tucker is unlikely to offer much in the way of fantasy value given his limited offensive upside.

Girgensons will miss his second straight game, but he might be ready to return against Carolina on Wednesday. He has contributed one goal, three assists, 26 shots on net, 15 blocked shots and 56 hits in 18 appearances this season.

Geekie has missed the last two games after landing on injured reserve, and he is facing an extended absence. He has earned four goals, five points, 27 shots on net and 59 hits in 20 outings this season.

Hagel was expected to miss a second consecutive game Thursday against the Oilers, and his placement on injured reserve means that he'll also be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Sabres. He was previously considered day-to-day due to his lower-body injury, so it's possible that he's in the mix to return Wednesday against the Hurricanes, but Jansen Harkins was recalled from AHL Syracuse to provide additional depth in Hagel's absence.

Sissons still needs to be cleared for contact, but he will participate in Sunday's practice. He has missed the last six games, but he has been making progress in his recovery. Sissons has two goals, six points, 19 shots on net, 38 hits and 11 blocked shots in 19 appearances this season.

Roslovic earned an assist, two hits and one blocked shot in 15:04 of ice time against Columbus on Saturday. He has earned an assist in three straight games. Rosolvic has registered nine goals, 23 points, 61 shots on net, 18 hits and 10 blocked shots in 24 appearances this season. It's unclear if he will be available for Monday's matchup against the Islanders.

Marchenko will wear a non-contact jersey during the morning skate, so a return to the lineup against the Blue Jackets on Saturday appears unlikely. He has missed the last 10 games, but seems to be progressing. Marchenko has earned six goals, 14 points, 35 shots on net and 20 hits in 14 appearances this season.
The Maple Leafs moved McWard onto the injured reserve list Friday. He hasn't picked up a point in two NHL outings this season, but he has earned one shot on net, three blocked shots and one hit.

Blankenburg is expected to participate in Saturday's morning skate, but it's unclear when he will be ready to return to the lineup. He is currently on injured reserve and hasn't played since Oct. 22. Blankenburg has one goal, six shots on net, six hits and two blocked shots in six appearances this campaign.

This move was necessary to create cap space for the activation of Dakota Joshua (abdomen) from LTIR. Wood has had no established timeline for a return, but he will be required to miss at least three more games.

There's no timetable for Domi's return after he had complications while undergoing surgery over the summer. The 31-year-old had 12 goals, 36 points and 95 PIM in 80 regular-season appearances with Toronto in 2025-26. Domi will likely serve in a middle-six capacity once he's ready to return.

Less than 24 hours after Merzlikins was traded to the Maple Leafs, a timetable for his return to action has been provided. The 32-year-old backstop had an up and down season in 2025-26, where he posted a 14-11-3 record, a 3.39 GAA and an .883 save percentage across 30 regular-season outings. He won't be rushed into action, as the Leafs new goaltender tandem of Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz are still expected to handle the majority of reps between the pipes this upcoming season. However, when Merzlikins is ready to return, he's the clear No. 3 option in Toronto's organization and could still see some playing time at the NHL level if he isn't sent down to AHL Toronto.
day-to-day

Marino has two goals and five points in nine appearances with Utah in 2026-27. When he's ready to return, Marino will probably serve in a top-four capacity, while Zac Jones or Nick DeSimone will likely shift out of the lineup.

Guenther didn't take regular line rushes at Friday's practice, but he could be nearing a return to action. Prior to his five-game absence, the 23-year-old winger notched two goals and one assist, all with the man advantage, in his last seven outings. Once given the green light to play, Guenther should resume his spot in the top six as well as seeing power-play minutes.

The Mammoth indicated Monday that Schmidt was considered out indefinitely, and he was officially placed on injured reserve. It isn't particularly surprising to see him labeled as week-to-week, and it indicates that he's unlikely to return after spending the minimum amount of time on IR. It seems likely that the 35-year-old will be sidelined until at least late November.

Pettersson has already been ruled out for Saturday's matchup against Minnesota, and the Canucks will be cautious with the 28-year-old forward. It's still unclear when he will be ready to return. Pettersson has provided six goals, 23 points, 30 shots on net, 32 blocked shots and 41 hits in 24 appearances this season.

Gallagher will miss at least the next three games, starting with Saturday's matchup against Minnesota, but it's unclear when he will be ready to return. He has collected three assists, 26 shots on net, eight blocked shots and 32 hits in 21 appearances this campaign.

Demko missed the second half of the 2025-26 season after undergoing hip surgery in January, and he was officially placed on injured reserve last week. He doesn't yet have a clear timetable for when he'll be back in action, but Sedin said that Demko is "taking steps every day" in his recovery process. While Demko is sidelined, Kevin Lankinen and Leevi Merilainen should compete for starts in the Canucks' crease.

It seems unlikely Desharnais will immediately return to the lineup against the Bruins on Saturday, though he seems to be making progress in his recovery. The 30-year-old blueliner has been sidelined for the Caps' last 11 games. Prior to getting hurt, Desharnais failed to score a goal in nine outings while chipping in three assists, three shots and 22 hits.

Sandin has yet to get into a game this year while recovering from knee surgery, but he seems to be getting closer to suiting up for the Caps -- though he won't play during the trip. In 73 regular-season games last year, the 26-year-old blueliner recorded five goals, 24 assists and 90 shots on goal while averaging 19:12 of ice time.

DeMelo has already been placed on injured reserve, but this latest update provides a clearer recovery timeline. The blueliner hasn't scored a goal since Opening Night versus Boston, a stretch of 19 games without finding the back of the net. During that stretch, DeMelo did chip in seven helpers, 27 hits and 22 blocks, giving him decent category coverage in banger formats.

Bjugstad underwent surgery to repair a torn left pectoral muscle in September, and he was transferred to long-term injured reserve in early October. The 34-year-old isn't expected to be in the mix to return to game action until at least January, but he'll likely have the chance to compete for a bottom-six role once he's cleared to suit up.
